claim: The compatible-set posterior used by S2 is exact: integer counts over intermediate states agree with brute-force enumeration
scope: 1,160 random small-space queries (n=3-4, h=0-3, edit/clamp/none, compound predicates); 0 mismatching (num,den)
limitations: h<=3 implemented; larger h falls back to SAT/enumeration

claim: Exact verdicts (Boolean support h=1, integer counts h<=3) agree with complete SAT verdicts
scope: S2-dev-v2 B16 primary regime: 14,880 queries, 0 mismatches; review tautology now entailed
limitations: finite corpus

claim: S2 design v2 is exogenous: hidden-mechanism swaps leave every measurement/query specification identical
scope: review repro inverted; all regimes' ex ante specifications
limitations: observational/clamp trajectories still follow the mechanism (their own public history), by design

claim: REVISED PRIMARY (development): no clear index-code advantage over the compatible-set majority in structured worlds
scope: 250 structured worlds, B16, 16 intervention queries: +0.0009 [-0.0111, +0.0121]
limitations: development salt; does not show equivalence; does not refute simplicity priors generally

claim: HISTORICAL secondary: index beats a uniformly random compatible model
limitations: beaten by majority by the same margin; mostly reflects the weak comparator

claim: Under the uniform-H null the majority beats index selection, as the Bayes argument predicts
scope: null 250 worlds: index - majority -0.0217 [-0.0325, -0.0111]; exhaustive n=3,k=1 (512 networks x 3 budgets) majority >= index and >= random on average
limitations: individual worlds can favour index

claim: Circuit-code selection beats the majority in structured worlds, concentrated in XOR-generated families
limitations: generator/code alignment, not an index-method result

claim: EXPLORATORY: index selection loses less to the majority in structured than in null worlds
limitations: not a superiority claim for the index code; exploratory interaction

claim: A finite-sample MC majority is unreliable only through exact ties; no predeclared budget reaches 0.002 contrast precision
scope: 200 worlds x 16 queries x 3 budgets x 4 streams: non-tie flips <=5/~6,000; world-level contrast shift 0.004-0.006 at every budget
limitations: diagnostic of the comparator, not of the hypothesis

claim: The v1 index-majority estimate was not an MC artefact: exact re-scoring gives +0.0055 (tie->0) / +0.0024 (half credit) vs +0.0065 MC
scope: 250 v1 structured worlds, 4,000 queries, 0 truth mismatches, 14 decision flips, 215 exact ties
limitations: v1 design remains mechanism-dependent (R02 not repaired by re-scoring)

claim: Noise handling comes from the two-part residual code, not uniquely from the index code
scope: 50 noise worlds: two-part MDL for index/circuit/bdd/dnf under identical residual model; e.g. rate 0.05 B32: circuit 0.948, index 0.910, bdd 0.911, dnf 0.874
limitations: descriptive

claim: Production S1 backends agree with the exhaustive reference on new development worlds after runner/core repairs
scope: 98 new worlds; 1,152 reference comparisons per backend (index_cube 1,147); 0 mismatches; 0 cross-backend disagreements; 696 checked proofs + 1 uncertified UNSAT
limitations: counts of comparisons, not a universal proof; the 3/M per-query bound is withdrawn

claim: index_sat (hybrid) completed every development query up to n=256 within the 20 s cap
scope: S1 panel n=64/128/256: 240/240 each; median 0.020 s at n=256
limitations: hybrid with SAT, not pure index algebra; S1 query scaling, not S2 induction

claim: Decoder charge = complete local dependency bundle (18,339 B gzip-9), runnable with the standard library only
scope: codec+index_repr+schema; -I -S interpreter decodes all 7 codecs
